claude_code.supported_min_source: the .claude-plugin/marketplace.json schema this catalog ships has been stable since 2.0.0; the previous floor was never validated
claude_code.verification_method: Real direct CLI check this run — `claude --version` on the runner reports 2.1.251, the third consecutive run with a live CLI available, so `validated_against` and `latest_known` stay equal. `claude plugin validate --strict .agents/skills` was re-run against this live 2.1.251 CLI and passed clean, and `claude plugin marketplace add`-style catalog resolution was re-checked via `make validate` (regenerate + validate manifests; 3 plugins in sync, no drift). The 2.1.248 → 2.1.251 changelog delta (2.1.249/2.1.250 published no separate entry beyond "bug fixes and reliability improvements") was reviewed line-by-line against the catalog surface. Three items are directly about marketplace/catalog/worktree behavior and got a real check, not a rubber stamp: (1) 2.1.251's plugin-command path-traversal rejection (a marketplace entry's declared command could point outside the plugin directory; now rejected at load) — checked directly against `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`: none of this catalog's three plugin entries declare a `commands` field at all, so this catalog never exercised the vulnerable path; documented as confirmed not applicable. (2) 2.1.251's fix for background sessions occasionally starting with zero plugin skills (and staying that way) when another Claude Code process was refreshing the plugin marketplace at the same moment — directly relevant to any multi-session workflow that installs from this catalog while another session is also touching its marketplace cache; documented as a new Troubleshooting row. (3) 2.1.251's fix for `--worktree --tmux` against a `gitlab.com` origin trying a doomed GitHub-style fetch first instead of the GitLab ref directly — relevant to the GitLab-mirror guidance already in the install guide's plugin-sources section; documented there. Also checked: 2.1.248's MCP `headersHelper`-supplies-`Authorization` OAuth-discovery-on-401 fix (the helper is now re-run and the call retried on a 401, as originally documented) — directly relevant to the `headersHelper` capability this install guide already documents for a future private/token-gated entry; noted alongside it. And 2.1.248's `experimental.cacheTtl` agent-frontmatter setting — checked and not applicable, this catalog ships no agent definitions of its own (only a contributor skill). Everything else in 2.1.248–2.1.251 (`--restricted`, self-hosted-runner and `claude agents` UI/reliability fixes, cross-session messaging on Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry, `SendFeedback`-adjacent and spend-limit/`/cost`/`/usage` UI, model-switch hook events, Remote Control and cloud-session fixes, sandbox/security fixes unrelated to plugin commands, and terminal/UI polish) is host/CLI/session-side with no marketplace-manifest surface. Prior verification still holds: catalog install previously verified with `claude plugin marketplace add Tamircohen28/tamirs-marketplace` followed by `claude plugin install <name>@tamirs-marketplace`.

opencode.supported_min_source: oldest version on which `skills.paths` discovery of a catalog plugin's skills was verified with `opencode debug skill`
opencode.verification_method: opencode --version on the maintainer machine; latest from registry.npmjs.org/opencode-ai. OpenCode has no marketplace, so the catalog itself cannot be installed — each plugin repo is cloned and its skills verified with `opencode debug skill`

capability_gaps.marketplace: OpenCode has no plugin marketplace and no plugin manifest, so this catalog cannot be added as an install source. Each plugin repo is installed directly — clone it and point `skills.paths` at its `skills/` directory, or symlink it into the OpenCode skills directory. Every plugin in this catalog ships its own `opencode.json` and its own OpenCode install guide.
capability_gaps.catalog_discovery: There is no OpenCode equivalent of listing plugins from a remote catalog. The plugin table in this repo's README is the discovery surface; installation is then per-repo.
